title: Spike detection and bounded regression policy for Optimize evals
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Define deterministic rules and thresholds for Optimize eval runs to detect metric spikes, bound acceptable regressions, and automate canary termination or rollback. This ticket captures PRD-level requirements, sampling and prompt-set stratification, statistical decision logic, A/B criteria, and integration points for dashboards and alerts.
background: During recent model rollouts we observed short-lived metric spikes (quality and latency) that either self-resolved or presaged larger regressions. Current manual canary reviews are inconsistent: some regressions are allowed through due to insufficient sample stratification or lack of bounded rollback rules. Optimize needs a formal policy so that canaries are terminated automatically on high-confidence negative signals, but small noisy fluctuations do not trigger unnecessary rollbacks.
scope_inclusions: Prompt-set sampling policy (stratified by intent, length, domain, and frequency)
Per-eval metric guardrails and minimum detectable effect size (MDE)
Automatic canary termination rules for safety/quality regressions and operational spikes (latency/cost)
A/B analysis decision rules including sample size, significance, and minimum effect thresholds
Integration with Console dashboards and Alerting (PagerDuty/Slack) for triggered rollbacks
scope_exclusions: New model training or model architecture changes
Full redesign of the Optimize UI (only dashboard links and annotations required)
Changes to dedicated/private deployment networking or infra quotas
prompt_set_policy: Baseline prompt set = 5,000 examples per workload (generation/chat/rerank/embeddings) as default
Stratify samples by: user intent (support/creative/transactional), token length buckets (0-64,65-256,257+), customer tier (free/paid/enterprise), and domain (finance/health/tech/other)
Ensure at least 500 examples per stratum where traffic exists; if stratum < 500, mark as low-confidence and report with canary summary
Include 250 adversarial/failure-case prompts curated by applied ML for regressions in safety or hallucination
Random seed and sampling pipeline must be recorded and surfaced in canary run metadata for reproducibility
metrics_spec: Primary quality metric: weighted human preference win-rate vs baseline (win-rate aggregated across prompt-set with stratified weights)
Secondary metrics: factuality score (automated fact-checker pass rate), hallucination rate, toxicity score, and task-specific accuracy when available
Operational metrics: median p50 and p95 per-token latency, 95th percentile tail latency across tokens, and cost per 1k tokens (USD)
Composite health score: 60% quality, 25% latency, 15% cost normalized to baseline for quick gating decisions
Report all per-stratum metrics in addition to global aggregates
statistical_rules: Require both statistical confidence (two-sided tests, alpha=0.05) AND a minimum practical effect size before declaring a regression; default MDE = 1.5 percentage points absolute for win-rate unless workload-specific MDE configured
Use sequential testing correction: apply alpha spending with O'Brien-Fleming boundaries for canaries longer than 24h or Bonferroni correction across >5 simultaneous hypotheses
For small strata (<500 examples), use Bayesian credible intervals with 95% posterior mass to estimate direction and mark outcomes as low-confidence
Adjust for seasonality or traffic shifts by comparing to baseline windows matched on hour-of-week when possible

When multiple metrics disagree (e.g., quality down but latency improved), run pre-defined tie-breaker: prioritize user-facing quality over latency unless cost/latency regressions exceed severity thresholds
canary_config: Default traffic split for canary: 5% traffic, ramp allowed to 10% after 12 hours if no signals
Minimum canary runtime: 48 hours or until minimum sample size for MDE is reached (whichever is longer); for low-volume workloads extend to 7 days
Minimum public events per canary: 5,000 user-facing requests or 5,000 prompt-set evaluations (whichever is larger) before final decision
Allow manual override by on-call or release owner with reason; manual overrides must be annotated and audited
Canary should be deployed across at least two regions for latency/capacity signal detection where region routing is relevant
auto_rollback_rules: Immediate automatic rollback if any of the following are true with >= 97% confidence:
- Win-rate regression > 3 absolute percentage points AND p < 0.01
- Factuality or safety metric drops by > 2 absolute percentage points AND credible interval excludes no-change
- Operational spike: p95 latency increases by > 60% compared to baseline or cost-per-token increases by > 50%

Automatic rollback also triggers if 2 or more medium regressions occur across different families (quality + latency, or quality + safety) even if individually below immediate thresholds, provided combined composite health score falls below 0.85 of baseline

Soft-stop canary (pause traffic) if signals are ambiguous but trending negative: pause at 2x SE of baseline and notify owners; resume only after manual review or after automatic testing window completes
Rollbacks must include post-rollback verification run (smoke eval on baseline prompt set) and automated incident ticket creation with attached canary run summary
monitoring_and_alerting: Add prebuilt dashboard tile: canary health summary with per-metric CI bands, per-stratum breakdown, and composite health score
Alerting rules: high-severity PagerDuty if auto-rollback fires; medium-severity Slack channel alert for pause/soft-stop events
On-call playbook link must be included in alert payload with checklist: reproduce, annotate, triage, rollback rationale
Log retention: keep canary run metadata and prompt sampling seeds for 90 days; longer retention (1 year) for enterprise customers behind support agreement
Post-mortem template auto-created when rollback occurs with fields: root cause hypothesis, action items, test coverage gaps
acceptance_criteria: An implementation plan exists that maps the PRD rules to the Optimize service APIs and Console signals (owner: Eng-SRE)
Prompt-set sampling code integrated with existing eval pipelines and exposes stratum-level sample sizes and random seeds
Dashboards show per-canary CI bands, composite health score, and the automatic decision output (pass/pause/rollback)
Automated rollback/pause executions are wired to the deployment system with safe rollback validation and audit logs
Runbook and PagerDuty alerts created and tested in staging with simulated regressions
A/B analysis module can compute MDE, apply sequential correction, and produce a human-readable verdict with links to raw samples
Documentation and onboarding doc for PM/SE on how to interpret canary outputs and request manual overrides
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Decided to require both statistical significance and minimum effect size to avoid noisy triggers (Aisha, Marcus, Priya)
2026-03-04: Chose stratified sampling by intent/length/domain with 5k baseline size after simulation results from Applied ML (Marcus, Jonah)
2026-03-06: Agreed to composite health score weighting (60% quality / 25% latency / 15% cost) for quick gating; final weights may be tuned after 2 months of telemetry (Product + ML)
2026-03-09: Auto-rollback thresholds tightened for safety/factuality metrics following legal/security review (no-regression tolerance tightened)
notes: Follow-up: run A/A experiments for 2 weeks to validate false positive rate of auto-rollback rules (owner: Applied ML)
Edge case: for enterprise customers with custom prompt sets, default MDE may be relaxed if customer defines bespoke acceptance criteria (product-led config)
Consider adding an emergency 'freeze' flag that allows cross-team pause of all canaries during incidents (requires engineering guardrails)
